gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many days each kit carries a stated outage load with its own panels deployed (battery Wh ÷ (daily load − daily panel harvest)), or the panel wattage at which that load is covered: about 860 W for Lights On Labs' 3,284 Wh/day essentials list at StormWatts' 4.5 sun-hours × 0.85.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), Lights On Labs, Solar Gen Advisor, Prepared States, the Anker SOLIX kit collection (cited) and our own under-$3,000 page; powersized.com could not be opened (certificate error). StormWatts gives $/kWh and percent refilled on a 4.5-sun-hour day, and says it never states days at a daily load or a break-even panel wattage. Lights On Labs gives the 3,284 Wh/day load, battery-only hours and '400 W would need 8.2 hours', but no net-days figure. Solar Gen Advisor gives harvest per day and fridge hours as separate figures, and has no kit above 2,765 Wh. Prepared States lists price, Wh and panel watts only. The ingredients exist on rival pages; the combined figure and the 860 W threshold do not.
decides: It moves the pick away from the 400 W kits ChatGPT led with: on paper they last about 2 days on that load (F3000 + 400 W 1.8, DELTA Pro 3 + 400 W 2.3, HomePower 3600 Plus + 2× 200 W 2.0). Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2× 400 W at $3,599.99 lasts about 22 days on the same arithmetic and is the pick if it ships now. That needs a recheck: Anker's S5000 page today says orders placed on or after November 6 ship in 11-12 weeks, while our kit table says ships now. If it is not shipping, the ships-now rows under $4,000 are ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP039 600 W ($1,753.93, 3.2 days) and the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit + 2× 100 W ($3,799.05, 2.0 days). For a shopper who can wait, BLUETTI Apex 200 + B500K + 2× 500 W ($3,986.20 through our link, store $4,196, late January 2027) is the only row under budget with both 1,000 W of panels and the largest battery (7,680 Wh, $0.52/Wh); its harvest exceeds the load on paper.

findings.label: Panel watts needed to cover the essentials load each day
findings.source_title: Best solar generators for home backup (2026) | Lights On Labs
findings.note: 3,284 Wh ÷ (4.5 h × 0.85) = 858.6 W. Under budget, only the 1,000 W kits clear it; 800 W falls 224 Wh a day short; 400 W covers 1,530 Wh, 47% of the load. Arithmetic at StormWatts' mid-case sun; winter output is lower.

findings.label: Days on the 3,284 Wh/day load with its own panels
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 + 400W Bifacial Solar Panel - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: 800 W × 3.825 = 3,060 Wh/day; 3,284 − 3,060 = 224 Wh/day short; 5,024 Wh ÷ 224 = 22.4 days. Rated battery Wh, no inverter loss. Very sensitive to sun: at Solar Gen Advisor's planning figures (4 h × 0.75 = 2,400 Wh/day) it is 5,024 ÷ 884 = 5.7 days. 5,024 Wh is from the project kit table; Anker's page says '5kWh'.
